recognize_zh: 薄層血液抹片中有兩個瘧原蟲裂殖體（schizont）：右上方一個在藍色細胞質內含約 8 個分散的紫紅色染色質點（merozoite），中央一個則是更緻密、塞滿染色質顆粒的成熟裂殖體；但被感染紅血球未見明顯變大，也看不到 Schüffner 小點，種別無法僅憑本圖確認為間日瘧（P. vivax）。
features: Two intraerythrocytic parasites with multiple discrete magenta chromatin dots (merozoites), consistent with schizonts
Upper parasite: about 8 separate chromatin dots within blue parasite cytoplasm, an early-to-mid schizont
Central parasite: densely packed merozoites filling the parasite with dark granular material, a mature schizont; merozoites too crowded to count reliably
Host red cells are not appreciably enlarged and Schüffner stippling is not seen at this magnification
Background erythrocytes show crenated (echinocytic) and irregular forms, likely drying artifact; scattered platelets
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows two intraerythrocytic malaria parasites at the schizont stage, one containing approximately eight discrete chromatin dots in blue cytoplasm and the other a mature schizont densely filled with merozoites. The infected red cells do not appear enlarged relative to surrounding erythrocytes, and Schüffner stippling is not evident; background red cells show crenation artifact. Because the classic P. vivax features of host-cell enlargement, stippling and 12-24 merozoites cannot be confirmed in this field, species assignment should rely on the full smear, other stages and PCR or antigen testing. Findings are consistent with malarial schizonts, compatible with but not specific for Plasmodium vivax.

ddx.vs: P. malariae schizonts have 6-12 merozoites often in a rosette with coarse central pigment in normal-sized or small red cells without stippling.
P. falciparum schizonts are rarely seen in peripheral blood and are accompanied by many small delicate rings, multiply infected cells and crescent-shaped gametocytes.
P. ovale has 6-14 merozoites in enlarged oval red cells with fimbriated edges and prominent Schüffner (James) dots.
A superimposed platelet shows fine azurophilic granules in a pale gray matrix without discrete chromatin dots in blue parasite cytoplasm and lies in a different focal plane.
